svg.title: Complete parameter boxes and a common value
svg.desc: Schematic nested closed parameter rectangles C n times D n inside a product of complete metric spaces. Both parameter diameters tend to zero. The product maps by alpha times beta to a metric target square. Its images approach the diagonal by a uniform error tending to zero. The parameter limits therefore have equal images. The target need not be complete. Incomplete parameters, nonclosed boxes and escaping boxes give separate counterexamples.
svg.text: Find the limits in the parameter spaces
α : P → Y; β : Q → Y, continuous
P and Q are complete; Y is a metric space.
Nested closed boxes in P × Q
C₁ × D₁
C₂ × D₂
Schematic only; the factors need not be intervals.
α × β
The image pair approaches the diagonal
dᵧ(α(p), β(q)) ≤ εₙ → 0
For every p ∈ Cₙ and q ∈ Dₙ.
No new target point is obtained by completing Y.
Three ways to lose the parameter pair
Incomplete P, Q: the limit lies outside them.
Nonclosed Cₙ, Dₙ: their boundary limit is lost.
No shrinking diameter: the parameters escape.
Exercise 7.9 keeps the target complete in every case.
Small image distance alone supplies no parameter limit.
